◆ The whole fortnight in 60 seconds

Week 40, bonds: the 10-year reached 5.36%, its highest since 2002, then failed there twice. The 10-year auction drew the strongest demand since 2016. Yields closed the week 2 bp lower. Our gate “the 10-year back under 5.25% after the auctions” passed on Thursday.

Week 40, war and AI: oil swung on Iran headlines all week. On Thursday Trump said the US will not attack Iran before the 3 November midterms, and oil dropped about $1.50 in minutes. A report that OpenAI’s revenue run-rate was near $50B knocked chips 3.4%, then a guide of at least $70B repaired it. The S&P 500 made a record at 7,846.6.

Week 40, our book: SPX A paid all three targets, Gold B and GBPJPY A paid target 1, Gold A and BTC B were stopped. Your own four trades closed about +7.9R.

Week 41: CPI week. Core at 0.2% or softer (our call) breaks the 10-year under 5.20%, tips the dollar out of its supply zone and shifts gold above 4,210. A hot print sends us to deeper buy levels at half size. Either way we buy levels, not spikes.

00WEEKEND UPDATE

The weekend wire, graded against our map

10-SECOND VERSIONThe weekend brought attacks near Saudi Arabia, Iraq and the UAE, but none of them stopped oil flowing. That is noise for prices until a strait closes or US forces strike. CPI on Wednesday is still the main event.
◎ In plain words

Markets are closed on the weekend, but the news is not. Each Sunday we sort the weekend headlines into six grades: tailwind (helps our trades), real risk (could change our plan), hot watch (not yet, but close), priced (already in the price), theatre (loud words, no action) and noise. Then we check every trade idea against the latest price, so you know which ones are close before Monday opens.

Countdown to CPI

Wednesday 14 October, 08:30 ET (12:30 UTC). Core CPI forecast 0.2%, prior 0.3%. FEED [11][9]

The weekend wire

FRI 9 OCT · LATEHOT WATCHOILXAU

Riyadh airport attack, explosions in Erbil, a vessel struck off the UAE

The EU expressed “full solidarity” after the deadly attack on Riyadh’s airport. The UK’s maritime agency reported a vessel struck 13 nautical miles west of Al Jazeera, UAE. Explosions were reported in Erbil, Iraq.
OUR READ These hit airports and shipping, not Gulf oil output, and no US forces struck back. Price shrugged: WTI +0.4%, gold −0.1% on the headlines. Hot watch, not a trigger [10]
THIS WEEKHOT WATCHOILDXY

About 9,000–10,000 US personnel heading to the region

The USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier group and the USS Makin Island amphibious group are deploying. Trump has said no strikes on Iran before 3 November.
OUR READ Forces moving in while the President pledges no strikes until after the midterms: the risk is pushed to November, not removed. That is why the defense board keeps “US strikes on Iran” as the hot-watch trigger [31][15]
FRI 9 OCTTAILWINDXAUOIL

Gold +1% on easing oil and a softer dollar; Germany to release up to 15M barrels

Germany will release up to 15 million barrels under the G7 stock accord, on top of the 100 million barrels the G7 agreed the previous weekend.
OUR READ Lower oil means less inflation fear, which means lower yields, which is what gold needs. This is the Gold engine’s tailwind [10][1]
FRI 9 OCT · 08:30 ETPRICEDCAD

Canada lost 68,300 jobs against a forecast of +9,200; unemployment 6.5%

Full-time jobs fell 35,400. Participation 64.8%.
OUR READ Bad for the Canadian dollar, but USDCAD only rose to 1.4299 because the US dollar was already stuck at supply. We sell USDCAD only once the dollar turns [11][24]
THIS WEEKPRICEDJPY

US and Japanese finance chiefs in Bangkok for the IMF and G20

Bessent, Katayama and Ueda are all in Bangkok. Japanese investors bought ¥1.32 trillion of foreign stocks last week.
OUR READ Talk about a “desirable” strong yen is possible, but the flow that matters (Japanese money into US stocks) is still coming. Fade yen spikes, do not chase them [42][23]

Every Week 41 idea against the latest price

Distance from the near edge of each zone. “Daily moves” divides the distance by the asset’s usual daily move (20-day volatility), so you can compare gold with Bitcoin fairly.

◆ Our read

Nothing that happened over the weekend reached the bar for a defense trigger. The ideas closest to price are Gold B (the retest box only goes live after a 4H close above 4,210), GBPJPY A and BTC A. Everything else needs CPI to move price to it first.

✓ Why it matters

Most traders start the week reacting to the loudest weekend headline. Grading the wire first stops you from changing a good plan because of noise.

A tanker is struck off the UAE but oil barely moves. Which grade does it get, and why?
Hot watch. It is the kind of event that could matter (Gulf shipping), but price did not reprice it and no oil supply was lost. It becomes a trigger only if traffic through Hormuz stops or energy infrastructure is hit.

01WEEK 40 IN ONE FRAME

Two stories: bonds topped, the war premium faded

10-SECOND VERSIONLong-term US interest rates hit a 24-year high and could not go higher. Then the President said no Iran strikes before the election. Lower rates and calmer oil lifted stocks and gold.
◎ In plain words

Two things drove almost every move. Story 1, the bond market: the 10-year yield (what the US government pays to borrow for ten years) touched 5.36% on Wednesday, the highest since 2002. Big buyers then showed up at the auctions, and the yield failed at the same high on Thursday. Story 2, the war: headlines about possible US strikes on Iran pushed oil up, and Trump’s pledge on Thursday pushed it down. When yields and oil fall together, stocks and gold usually rise. That is what happened on Thursday and Friday.

Day by day

MON 5Soft growth, hot pricesISM services 54.9 but its prices index 74. The G7’s 100M-barrel release and a Saudi price cut sent WTI −2.5%. SPX +0.6% to 7,776. [1]
TUE 6Record highSPX touched about 7,840. The BoJ’s Ueda signalled no October hike (odds fell to about 12%). The dollar slipped to 101.8. [2]
WED 7The yield high and the gold grab10-year 5.36% at 09:25 ET. Gold fell $33 in five minutes to the 4,067 low and was bought. The 10-year auction drew record non-dealer demand. FOMC minutes: all 19 backed September’s hike. [3][8]
THU 8The pledgeStrike reports pushed WTI toward $94.80. The OpenAI revenue report hit chips −3.4%. At about 12:20 ET Trump said no attack on Iran before the midterms; oil −$1.50 in minutes. 10-year closed 5.23%. [4][15]
FRI 9Relief, then headlinesGold +1% to 4,209. Canada −68.3K jobs. OpenAI guided at least $70B; tech rebounded. Late: Riyadh, Erbil, a UAE vessel. Price shrugged. [10]

Reading the tape

WED
Gold −$33 in five minutes with no headline

What price was saying: A liquidity grab. Stops under 4,100 were the fuel; big buyers used them as their fill and gold was back above 4,100 within the hour.

What the rules said to do: Gold A (4,107–4,121) was stopped. Gold B (4,055–4,076) triggered on the reclaim and later paid 4,200.

THU
Stocks fell on AI news, then rose on war news

What price was saying: The AI scare was about one company’s revenue, not AI demand. The pledge changed the inflation path for everyone.

What the rules said to do: Buy the S&P at the level, not after the headline. Your second S&P trade did exactly that.

FRI
Attacks in three countries, price shrugged

What price was saying: The market now prices the war on oil supply only. Shipping and airport attacks without supply loss do not move it.

What the rules said to do: Hot watch, no action.

◆ Our read

Week 40’s question was “can the bond market carry the supply?” The answer was yes: record demand at the 10-year auction and a solid 30-year. That removed the main brake on the AI trade and handed control to the data. Week 41’s question is simpler: does inflation agree?

✓ Why it matters

When you know which story moved a market, you know which news can move it back. Gold this week will move on yields (CPI), not on Gulf shipping headlines.

Oil fell and yields fell on Thursday. Why did both help gold?
Lower oil lowers expected inflation; lower yields lower the return on cash and bonds. Gold pays no interest, so when yields fall the cost of holding it falls and buyers come back.
DEEP DIVE
Why record auction demand mattered more than the Fed minutes

The Fed minutes said all 19 officials backed September’s hike and most expected another by year end. That is hawkish, and yet markets barely moved. The reason: futures already priced an October hold at about 80% and a December hike at about 75%. The minutes told the market what it already believed.

The auction was new information. A bid-to-cover of 2.77 (the highest since 2016) and 97.5% of the $39B taken by non-dealers (a record) said real investors want US debt at 5.3%. That caps the “fiscal sell-off” fear that had pushed long yields up for weeks, which is why the yield turned within minutes of the 13:00 ET result [3][5][30].

02THE RECEIPTS

Every Week 40 call and idea, scored

10-SECOND VERSIONOf 15 planned ideas, 5 triggered: 3 paid and 2 were stopped. On the plan’s own management that banked about +4.2R, with two runners still open. Seven ideas never reached their zones, which is the plan working: no zone, no trade.
◎ In plain words

A call is a view (“the auctions will be clean”). An idea is a trade plan with a zone, a stop and targets. We score both against what price actually did, using the plan’s own rules: the entry only counts if the trigger printed, and half comes off at target 1 with the stop moved to breakeven.

6 / 9calls passed
1 / 9mixed
2 / 9missed
+4.2Rideas, banked on plan

The calls

01“Clean auctions and the 10-year back under 5.25% unlock the buy zones”PASS

10-year auction 5.30%, bid-to-cover 2.77; 30-year 5.618%, 2.54 vs about 2.41 average. The 10-year closed Thursday at 5.23%. SPX A filled Monday and ran to the record [3][4].

02“AI race and yen carry: attack at the key zones”PASS

SPX record 7,846.6; GBPJPY A paid target 1 (209.50). Bitcoin was the exception (see 06).

03“The dollar: defense until the structure is clear”PASS

DXY ran to 102.54, an 18-month high, and EURUSD to a 17-month low. Defense kept us out of EURUSD A, which would have been stopped (low 1.1166 under the 1.1185 stop).

04“Gold: patience, build slowly above 4,090 or after a flush into 3,950–4,000”MIXED

The flush came, but only to 4,067, not 4,000. Gold A was stopped by it; Gold B caught it and paid 4,200. The idea of buying a flush was right; the depth was wrong.

05“Iran’s reply can gap oil and gold; do not chase a Monday gap”PASS

WTI opened near $93.65 Sunday and fell 2.5% Monday on the G7 release. Chasing the gap would have lost.

06“Bitcoin through the 87,319 double top confirms 88.6–89K”MISS

High 86,991, then $400M of leveraged longs were liquidated in an hour on Tuesday night and Bitcoin swept to 80,316. Bitcoin traded as weak tech beta, not as the AI engine’s leader [3].

07“The Fed minutes confirm one and done”MISS

All 19 officials backed September’s hike and most saw another by year end. The market ignored it: October hold odds stayed near 80–85% [8][3].

08“No entries on the auction and minutes candles”PASS

The 13:00 ET 10-year result moved yields 3 bp in minutes; the minutes moved nothing. The lock cost nothing and avoided the auction whip.

09“War on ice; oil premium fades”PASS

Oil spiked Thursday on strike reports, then the pledge took the premium out. WTI −0.35% on the week, Brent +0.8%.

◆ Our read

The plan earned its money in the places it was patient: SPX A only at the exact Monday low, Gold B only after the sweep, GBPJPY only on the reclaim. The two losses were both entries above an obvious level that a sweep then cleared.

✕ The common mistake

Counting “not filled” ideas as failures. An idea that never reaches its zone costs nothing. Seven of fifteen ideas did nothing this week, and that is a feature: we only trade where we planned to.

✓ Why it matters

Scoring on the plan’s own rules (trigger, half at T1, breakeven) tells you whether the process works. Scoring on “was I right about direction” tells you nothing you can repeat.

Gold A and Gold B were in the same market, the same week. Why did one lose and the other win?
Gold A sat just under 4,121, where many traders put stops. Gold B sat below the obvious level, where the sweep ran to. When a sweep is likely, the better entry is under the obvious level, after the stops are taken.

03THE JOB BOARD

Eight gates: 4 confirmed, 1 partial, 3 denied

10-SECOND VERSIONThe bond gate and the dollar-defense gate passed. The Bitcoin and “one and done” Fed gates failed. Six new gates for CPI week tell us exactly what would make us bigger or smaller.
◎ In plain words

A gate is a yes-or-no test written before the week: “if this happens, we do that”. Each gate gets checked, and each one gets three lines: why it happened, what the early warning was, and the rule we keep.

New gates for Week 41

1 · Core CPI 0.2% or softer

Confirms if Wed 08:30 ET core m/m ≤ 0.2%. Opens SPX A, the gold shift and the dollar-down trades.

2 · The 10-year under 5.20%

Confirms if a daily close under 5.20%. That is gold’s confirmation; a close above 5.36% is a defense trigger.

3 · The dollar’s lower high

Confirms if DXY prints a 4H lower high under 102.28 after CPI. Unlocks EURUSD A and the USDCAD short.

4 · Gold shifts structure

Confirms if a 4H close above 4,210. Unlocks Gold B and moves gold to full attack.

5 · The S&P holds 7,700 into Friday

Confirms if no daily close under 7,700 through three data mornings. A close under 7,620 is a defense trigger.

6 · GBPJPY breaks and holds 210.20

Confirms if a 4H close above 210.20 that is not reversed within a day. Opens 211.5 and 212.5.

◆ Our read

Every confirmation came from our patience rules; every denial came from a destination we hoped for (87,319, “one and done”, 101.75). This week’s gates are all about levels we wait for, not destinations.

✓ Why it matters

Writing the gate before the week stops hindsight from rewriting your memory. You can only learn from a prediction you wrote down.

DXY’s week low was 101.754 and the gate said “under 101.75”. Confirmed or denied?
Denied. A gate is binary. If you round it in your favour once, you will round every gate in your favour.

◇ The four-question headline filter

1. Did barrels, rates or earnings change? If not, it is words. 2. Was it already priced? Check the market odds. 3. Did price follow through after 15 minutes? 4. Does it change one of our gates? Only a “yes” to question 4 changes the plan.

◆ Our read

The week’s biggest lesson: the war moved oil, but the bond market moved everything. CPI is a bond-market event, which is why it outranks every Iran headline this week.

✓ Why it matters

If you react to every red BREAKING banner you will trade 30 times a week and lose to costs. Sorting by impact cuts that to the three or four that matter.

Decision versus outcome

Good decision · good outcome

Gold 2: entered after the 4,067 sweep, on the reclaim of the 4,112–4,116 zone. S&P 2: entered at the 7,751–7,756 zone near Thursday’s 7,737 low. Trump’s pledge was the catalyst; the level was the edge.

Good idea · early entry

Gold 1: right zone, but entered at about 08:00 ET Wednesday, 25 minutes before the $33 drop, with a 7.3-point stop. Gold’s average hour that week moved more than that. S&P 1: right direction, but entered Thursday morning into the strike reports and the 12:45 ET OpenAI report.

◇ The one lesson

Let the sweep happen first. Both losses were entries just above an obvious level; both wins were entries after price swept that level and came back. Your own rule from the plan already says it: a 15-minute close back above the zone.

Attachment check

  • Did I re-enter gold because I was sure, or because the plan had a second zone? The plan. ✓
  • Did I size up after the first loss? No. ✓
  • Did I move a stop? No sign of it. ✓
  • Did a headline make me enter? S&P 1, partly. ✕
  • Did I take profit at the planned target? Yes, both. ✓
  • Did I trade on a release candle? Gold 1 was close. ~

How open profit leaked

Very little. Gold 2’s target (4,179) was hit and gold went on to 4,209 Friday; S&P 2’s target (7,805) was hit and the index went to 7,819. That is about 0.5–2.6R left on the table, a fair price for a planned exit. If you want the extra, use the plan’s method: half off at target 1, runner with the stop at breakeven.

◆ Our read

This is what a good week looks like: half the trades lost and the account grew almost 8R. Keep the risk fixed; do not let +7.9R raise the size on CPI morning.

✕ The common mistake

Thinking the two losses were bad trades. Both had good plans and lost 1R each, exactly as designed. The mistake to avoid is the timing, not the idea.

✓ Why it matters

A 50% win rate with 5R winners is a strong edge. The only thing that can break it is size creeping up after a good week.

Your win rate is 50%, wins average 4.95R and losses 1R. What is your expectancy per trade?
0.5 × 4.95 − 0.5 × 1.0 = +1.98R. Even at a 30% win rate you would still make +0.79R per trade with these winners.

08DATA DECODED

Four nowcasts: build the number before it prints

10-SECOND VERSIONWe think core CPI comes in at about 0.19%, so 0.2% or lower. Gasoline will make the headline look hot (about 0.5%), but that is expected. Tap − / + to make your own call.
◎ In plain words

CPI is a weighted average of hundreds of prices. If you know the latest signal for each big piece (rents, cars, insurance, airfares) and how much each piece weighs, you can estimate the total before it is released. That estimate is a nowcast. Each row below is one piece: its weight, the latest evidence, our projection and how much it adds. Change any projection and the nowcast updates.

◆ Worked example

The core pieces below add up to 77.4% of the basket. Shelter is 35.4 of that 77.4, about 46% of core. If shelter rises 0.22% this month, it adds 35.4 × 0.22 ÷ 77.4 ≈ +0.10 point to core: more than half of our 0.19% call on its own. Used cars weigh 1.9; at −0.6% they subtract only about 0.015 point. Big pieces with small moves matter more than small pieces with big moves.

✕ The common mistake

Reading a hot headline CPI as a hot inflation print. With gasoline up about 9% seasonally adjusted, a 0.5–0.6% headline is expected. The market will trade core against 0.2%.

◆ Our read

Shelter is cooling, used cars are falling, insurance is falling and last month’s phone-plan jump was a one-off. That is why we sit at 0.19%, under the 0.2% forecast. Thursday’s claims are our boldest call: 214K against 200K, driven by seasonal filings, the hurricane and rising continuing claims.

✓ Why it matters

A December Fed hike is priced at about 74.5%. A cool core forces it out of the price, which drops yields and the dollar. That single repricing is what every engine in MOD-07 is waiting for.

Raise shelter from +0.22% to +0.35% in the CPI matrix. What happens to the verdict?
The core nowcast climbs to about 0.24%, which rounds to 0.2% but sits right on the edge. Shelter is the swing factor: if you think rents re-accelerate, you should not be calling a cool print.

09MAIN THESIS · THE AI GREED TRAIN

The race keeps getting funded

10-SECOND VERSIONThe AI companies keep raising huge sums to build chips and data centres. A scare about OpenAI’s revenue lasted one day. The danger is not the AI story; it is the cost of borrowing to pay for it.
◎ In plain words

AI needs chips, power and data centres, and those cost hundreds of billions. Companies borrow to pay for them. As long as money is cheap enough and buyers keep lending, the spending continues and AI stocks rise. If borrowing gets too expensive (high yields, wide credit spreads), the train slows.

✓ Why it matters

10THE GATE

The 10-year double top, and gold’s trigger at 5.20%

10-SECOND VERSIONThe 10-year yield failed twice at 5.35%. A cool CPI that pushes it under 5.20% is the trigger for gold and the AI trade. A close above 5.36% is our biggest warning sign.
◎ In plain words

The 10-year yield is the “gate” every engine passes through. It sets mortgage rates, company borrowing costs and the return on cash. Gold, which pays nothing, competes with it directly. When the gate closes (yields up), gold and stocks struggle; when it opens (yields down), they run.

The five forces on the 10-year

  1. Inflation: CPI Wednesday, PPI Thursday.
  2. The Fed path: October hold 84.5%, December hike 74.5% FEED.
  3. Supply: auctions cleared at record demand.
  4. Oil: the war premium faded after the pledge.
  5. Global bonds: Japan and Europe yields high, pulling capital.

Gold versus the 10-year

20-day correlation −0.35: when the 10-year falls, gold tends to rise. Gold versus DXY is weaker at −0.19. That is why the yield, not the dollar, is gold’s trigger this week FEED [14].

◆ Our read

Double tops at multi-decade highs are rare and powerful. With auction demand proven, the next push lower needs only a soft inflation number. Our line: a daily close under 5.20% confirms; above 5.36% is defense trigger M2.

✓ Why it matters

One chart decides three engines. Watching the 10-year on CPI morning tells you within 15 minutes whether to execute the cool plan or the hot plan.

CPI is cool but the 10-year only falls to 5.22% and stops. Is gold B live?
Not yet. Gold B needs a 4H close above 4,210 in gold itself. The yield helps, but the trigger is on gold’s own chart.
Sources: [3] [4] [12] [14]
11THE YEN CARRY TRADE

Who keeps the carry alive, and where Japan steps in

10-SECOND VERSIONBorrowing yen cheaply and holding higher-yielding pounds or dollars pays every day. The US and Japan both want that flow to continue. We buy the dips and fade the spikes near 160.
◎ In plain words

The carry trade: borrow in a currency with low interest rates (yen), invest in one with higher rates (dollars, pounds, US stocks), and keep the difference. It works while the yen stays calm. The danger is Japan’s Ministry of Finance buying yen to stop it falling (intervention), which can move USDJPY 3–5 yen in hours.

Monday is a holiday for US bonds, so real price discovery starts Tuesday with the banks. Wednesday is the main event. Thursday has four releases at once: expect a messy first hour.

✓ Why it matters

Most avoidable losses happen in the minute before a release. Knowing the exact time in your own zone stops you from being in a trade by accident.

Why does a 0.2% core CPI count as “cool” when the forecast is 0.2%?
On its own, 0.2% is in line. We call it cool because the range tops out at 0.6% and markets price a December hike; in-line keeps the cooling trend from PCE. The surprise is what moves price, so an in-line print hands control back to the levels.

13THE CPI MORNING

The 08:30 protocol: four outcomes, one plan each

10-SECOND VERSIONDo nothing for 15 minutes after 08:30 ET. Then read the 10-year and the dollar, pick one of four outcomes, and execute only that plan.
◎ In plain words

The first minutes after a big release are the most dangerous of the week: spreads widen, prices jump both ways, and stops get hit on noise. Professionals wait for the first 15-minute candle to close and then act on a plan written the night before.

08:25 Flat or at breakeven. Alerts set at every zone.
08:30 Read core m/m against 0.2%. Do not trade.
08:45 First 15-minute candle closes. Check the 10-year and DXY.
08:45+ Execute one plan below at the levels, not at market.

A · Cool double (core ≤ 0.1%)

10-year under 5.20% fast. Gold to 4,210 and beyond: wait for the 4H close, then Gold B. SPX A on any pullback. DXY lower high: EURUSD A and the USDCAD short go live.

B · Our call (core 0.2%, soft details)

10-year −1 to −3 bp. The pullback buys: SPX A, NAS A, GBPJPY A, USDJPY A. Gold builds; the shift may wait for PPI.

C · In line, mixed details

Control returns to structure. Trade the levels as written; the two-hour swing is noise inside the ranges.

D · Hot (core ≥ 0.3%)

Defense trigger M1 (+2 pts): half size. Wait for SPX B (7,610–7,625), Gold A (4,060–4,085), BTC B, GBPJPY B. Fade any USDJPY spike into 160.

◆ Our read

Gold has averaged a 0.48% swing in the first two hours of CPI mornings, the S&P about 0.24% and Bitcoin about 0.67% FEED. A stop inside that swing is a donation.

✕ The common mistake

Buying the first green candle at 08:30. The first move after CPI reverses often enough that it is not a signal. Your Gold 1 trade last week was entered minutes before a $33 drop: same lesson.

✓ Why it matters

Four outcomes, written in advance, turn a stressful morning into a checklist.

Core prints 0.2%, but the 10-year rises 4 bp in the first 15 minutes. Which plan?
Treat it as C: the details were not as soft as the headline number. Trade only the levels; do not force the cool plan.
Sources: [14] [34]

Risk-reward and size calculator

◆ Our read

Every plan clears 1:3 at target 1. Two ideas per market at most, and never both on the same day: A or B.

✕ The common mistake

Treating the projected candles as a forecast. They are drawings of two plans. Price will do something else in the details; the levels are what we trade.

✓ Why it matters

Seeing both CPI paths on the chart before Wednesday means you have already decided what to do in either case. On the morning you only have to recognise which one is happening.

Gold A shows 29% touch odds over 5 sessions. Should you move the zone closer to price?
No. The zone is where discount buyers acted last week. Low odds mean you will often not get the trade, which is fine: the reward when you do (up to 13.7R) is why it is worth waiting for.

15CORRELATION MAP

Which market pushes which, right now

10-SECOND VERSIONGold moves opposite the 10-year yield. Bitcoin moves with the Nasdaq. EURUSD moves opposite the dollar. These links change over time; check them before stacking trades.
◎ In plain words

Correlation runs from −1 (always opposite) to +1 (always together). Near 0 means no link. We use a 20-day rolling window, so the line shows how the link has changed over the last six months.

The correlation matrix, from real daily moves

◎ How to read it

Find a row and a column: the square where they meet is their link. Hover or tap a square for the exact value. Compare the 20- and 120-session views: when a colour flips, the relationship has changed recently, and trades built on the old link are riskier.

How one link changed over six months

PairWhat it means this week
Gold vs 10YA cool CPI that drops yields is gold’s best friend.
Bitcoin vs NasdaqBTC A and NAS A are partly the same trade: count them as one risk.
EURUSD vs DXYEURUSD A is a dollar trade; it needs the DXY trigger.
USDJPY vs 10YSoft yields dip USDJPY: that is the USDJPY A buy.
◆ Our read

Gold and the S&P both gain from lower yields this week. If you hold both, you have one bet on CPI, not two. Size accordingly.

✓ Why it matters

Hidden concentration is the most common way a good week turns into a bad one: three trades that are really one.

You are long BTC A and NAS A, 1% risk each. What is your real risk on a hot CPI?
Close to 2% on one outcome, because they move together (correlation about 0.6). Consider 0.5% each.

✕ The common mistake

Expecting the average. One CPI morning in three moves more than twice the average. The ±1σ whisker is there to remind you.

✓ Why it matters

If the simulator says gold should rise 0.2% and it falls 1%, something else is driving it. That is information you only have if you knew the normal reaction first.

Run “Replay · last CPI”. Did the markets follow the measured reaction?
Compare each bar with its violet marker. Where they disagree, another driver was in charge that day. That is why we wait 15 minutes and read the 10-year before acting.

FROM THE DESKWEEK 41 · CPI WEEK

Last week I took four trades: two losses and two wins, about +7.9R. Both wins came from waiting for the sweep and buying the level; both losses came from being early. The plan was right. My timing improved through the week.

I go into CPI with the same higher-timeframe view: the AI race is the modern industrial revolution, the yen carry stays on until something breaks, and gold is building after its discount demand held. PCE is trending lower, unemployment is higher, and the 10-year failed twice at its 2002 high. I expect softer CPI and PPI.

AI race and yen carry: attack at the key zones. Gold: discount buys, and full attack after the 4,210 shift. The dollar: defense until the lower high.

20EDUCATION

Eight CPI-week lessons

10-SECOND VERSIONHow CPI is built, why only the surprise matters, how to survive the first 15 minutes, and four calculators for odds, expectancy, drawdown and stop size.

How CPI is built

The Bureau of Labor Statistics prices about 80,000 items each month and weights them by how much households spend. Shelter is about a third of the whole basket and close to half of core. That is why rents decide core CPI more than anything else. Food and energy are left out of core because they jump around with weather and wars.

◆ Example

Gasoline weighs 3.2%. A 9% rise adds 3.2 × 9 ÷ 100 ≈ 0.29 point to the headline, which is why the headline forecast is 0.6% while core is 0.2%.

Surprise, not level

By Wednesday, the forecast is already in the price. A 0.2% core against a 0.2% forecast is zero surprise. Markets move on the difference between what prints and what was expected, and on the details (shelter, services) that show where the next one is going.

✕ Mistake

“Inflation is still 3.7%, so stocks must fall.” If 3.7% was expected, it is already in the price.

The first 15 minutes

At 08:30 liquidity thins, spreads widen and algorithms read the headline number in microseconds. The first move often reverses once humans read the details. Waiting for the first 15-minute candle to close costs a little of the move and saves a lot of whipsaws. See MOD-13 for the full protocol.

Touch odds

How likely is price to reach a level within a few sessions? With daily volatility σ, the chance of touching a level a distance d away within n days is about 2 × (1 − N(d ÷ (σ√n))). Try it:

Expectancy

Expectancy is what you make per trade on average: win rate × average win − loss rate × average loss. A 40% win rate is fine if winners are three times the losers.

Drawdown maths

Losses and gains are not symmetric. Lose 50% and you need +100% to get back. That is why the size rules exist.

ATR stops and sizing

The Average True Range (ATR) is the typical size of a candle. A stop inside one ATR is likely to be hit by noise. Set the stop in ATRs, then size the position so that stop equals your fixed risk.

Your Gold 1 stop was 7.3 points, about half of gold’s typical hourly range that week. That is why one wick took it out.

Monte Carlo: why a good week proves little

Four trades is a tiny sample. The Monte Carlo tool in MOD-06 replays a win rate and payoff 200 times in random order, showing the range of accounts the same edge can produce. With a 50% win rate and 5R winners, almost every path grows; drop the average win to 1.5R and watch the bands widen and the median flatten. Open the simulator ↗

Liquidity grabs

Stops cluster just beyond obvious levels. Large buyers need sellers to fill big orders; a fast push through the level triggers those stops and gives them the fill. The tell: a long wick through the level and a close back above it within the hour, exactly what gold did at 4,067 on Wednesday.

◇ The rule

Plan the entry after the grab: a 15-minute close back above the swept level. That is the difference between Gold A (stopped) and Gold B (paid).

Your account fell 25%. What gain do you need to get back to even?
25 ÷ 75 = +33.3%. Use the drawdown calculator to see how fast this grows.
21PSYCHOLOGY

Six rules for a data morning

10-SECOND VERSIONYour body reacts to the release before your plan does. Write the if-then the night before, halve the size after a stop, and do not let a good week raise your risk.
◎ In plain words

These rules come from studies of real traders and decision-making. Each one has a single action attached.

08:30 ET · The spike is not the signal

Professional traders’ heart rates and skin conductance jump on volatile events, even for veterans [34].

Rule: no entry until the first 15-minute candle after the print has closed.

Before the print · Write the if-then

Across 94 studies, “if X, then I do Y” plans clearly beat goals alone [35].

Rule: one line per asset: if cool I buy ___, if hot I buy deeper at ___.

After a stop · Losing mornings make reckless afternoons

Traders who lost in the morning took more risk in the afternoon and did worse [36].

Rule: after a stop on the print, half size or wait for London.

After +7.9R · Conviction in the call, discipline in the size

Wins get credited to skill, and size creeps up [37].

Rule: risk per trade stays fixed all October.

Swing holds · Stop checking the tick

The more often you look, the more losses you see and the earlier you bail [38].

Rule: check GBPJPY holds at session opens and on alerts only.

Double sessions · Sleep is position size

Sleep loss cuts judgment, and you will not notice [39].

Rule: under 6 hours of sleep caps size at half.
